text:
Marta (infra): FYI, getting reports that some clients for /dedicated-gpu are seeing the wrong cert in TLS handshake — CN shows *.staging.redwood-inference.internal instead of prod.
Jon (sre): when did this start? observed spike in TLS errors ~11:42 UTC?
Marta (infra): yep roughly 11:40-11:50 window. ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID from a subset of clients.
DeployBot: deploy canary dedicated-gpu v2.1.4 started at 11:37 UTC by Kevin (runtime)
Kevin (runtime): that canary patched the ALB annotations to reuse the existing listener (added alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/use-legacy-listener: "true") to avoid listener quota. Rolled to 25%.
Jon (sre): possible listener/conn reuse + cert rotation issue. Can we get describe-listeners for the prod ALB?
Marta (infra): pulling now...
Marta (infra): ```
aws elbv2 describe-listeners --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:XXX:loadbalancer/app/prod-alb/abcd1234
# Listener 443
DefaultAction: forward to tg-default
Certificates: [arn:acm:us-west-2:XXX:certificate/prod-cert]
Rules: HostHeader == staging.redwood-inference.internal -> forward tg-staging
       Path /dedicated-gpu -> forward tg-dedicated
```
Marta (infra): listener shows prod cert attached now, rules look sane.
NetOps: note — ALB can multiplex TLS connections and reuse sockets. If a cert was swapped on a listener during an active connection, some clients can be served from an unexpected session. SNI is set on handshake but persistent connections complicate things.
Jon (sre): do we have packet capture from an affected client?
Marta (infra): captured client-side tcpdump. ClientHello SNI: api.redwood-inference.com, ALPN: h2. Server sent the staging cert chain.
Kevin (runtime): ops ran a manual cert rotation script at 11:36 that temporarily attached a staging cert for a test validation, forgot to scope it to non-prod. That overlapped with the canary that told ingress to reuse the listener.
Ops: confirmed the rotation script attached arn:acm:.../staging-temp-cert at 11:36, then reattached prod at 11:52 after alerting.
Jon (sre): root cause hypothesis: manual cert swap -> canary reusing shared listener -> TCP/TLS connection reuse (HTTP/2 multiplexing) resulted in some clients receiving the previous cert when their request hit a reused, long-lived connection socket.
Kevin (runtime): mitigations: 1) reattach correct prod cert (done 11:52), 2) restart ingress pods to force new TLS handshakes (I triggered rolling restart), 3) pause the canary and rollback the listener reuse annotation (paused 11:55).
Marta (infra): I've also added a short script to perform a fresh TLS handshake smoke test after any cert attach — ensures CN/SAN match before marking rotation complete.
Jon (sre): additional ops knobs: set target group attribute to disable long lived keepalives for this path temporarily, consider disabling HTTP/2 on the ALB targets to avoid multiplexed sessions holding old state.
NetOps: note written for runbook about ALPN/h2 interactions and listener-level cert swaps. Also recommend tagging ACM certs with environment scope and refusing rotation if tags mismatch.
Ops: we'll update rotation script to check ACM tags and to perform an atomic swap guarded by a health-check probe that runs fresh handshakes.
Kevin (runtime): opening PR to remove alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/use-legacy-listener from the canary and to gate listener reuse behind an explicit rollout flag + test in CI.
Marta (infra): alerting: please add a monitor that fires when the certificate arn on the prod listener differs from expected arn:acm:.../prod-cert.
Jon (sre): playback: this was a race between a human-run cert rotation and an ingress canary that reused listeners; connection reuse + HTTP/2 multiplexing made some client sessions observe the temporary staging cert.
Marta (infra): error rate trending to baseline after 11:58; monitored TLS error counters back down.
DeployBot: canary paused by Kevin (runtime) at 11:55 UTC
Marta (infra): action items summarized: Kevin -> PR to rollback annotation + tests; Ops -> rotation script guard and ACM tag enforcement; SRE -> add cert-arn mismatch alert; NetOps -> update runbook on ALPN/session reuse and listener swap guidance; Infra -> add handshake smoke test post-rotation.
Jon (sre): one more: add a post-rotation check that makes a plain TCP connect with no keepalive to ensure new session, then validate cert CN/SAN and expiry.
Marta (infra): agreed. We'll document and run through a dry-run in staging before future cert ops. Closing thread, tracking follow-ups in #incidents. :white_check_mark:
